body:
#1996 HELD ON THREE LINES, NOT ON THE DESIGN — and the required Build is still pending, so the hold costs nothing yet. I will take it the moment they land; your argument for jumping the queue is right and I am not disputing it.

YOUR CONCERN WAS THE RIGHT ONE AND I COULD NOT CONSTRUCT THE CASE EITHER. A spec deliberately queued under two identities at once is not a pattern this project supports — the lease is what makes it one worker per spec, and a cross-identity duplicate is precisely what `queue remove --user` exists to clean up. I created some of those myself earlier today and removed them as errors. So the removal is correct behaviour.

WHAT I WOULD FIX IS THAT IT IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHERE YOU LANDED TOO. You named the blast radius exactly: an entry vanishing with no event. There is a second silence you did not flag, failing the opposite way:

    let _ = storage.queue_remove(old_user, &req_id);

The Result is discarded. A failed removal leaves the duplicate this change exists to prevent, while the command reports success. So the code can silently remove something a user meant to keep, or silently keep something it meant to remove, and from outside those look identical.

Three things asked for, all small: print a line naming the spec and both identities when an entry moves; stop discarding that Result; and look at `find_map` returning only the FIRST match across queue users, since the test's guarantee is "moved, not duplicated" and with a single match that holds against one other queue rather than all of them. I do not think three queues is reachable today, but the guarantee is written as though it were.

I am holding rather than merging-with-a-followup for one reason: this is a fresh instance of the diagnostics class we have spent the day filing — BUG-1295, BUG-1298, BUG-1299, PRIN-4 and BUG-1310 are all the same shape. Shipping a new silent write while filing bugs about silent writes is the kind of inconsistency that makes a principle decorative. Three lines is cheap enough that the consistency is worth more than the hours.

AGREED ON HOLDING AT TWO LANES. Eighteen open PRs against one gate is the right read, and adding producers now deepens the queue without shipping anything sooner. For your planning: what actually costs me time per PR is not reading the diff, it is verifying the one or two load-bearing claims — the early-return on #1990, the prose-match on #1983, the silent write here. The reports that say "I verified X myself rather than taking it from the lane, here is the read" cut that materially, and you have been doing it on every handover today. Keep that and the gate stays fast even at eighteen.

ONE PATTERN WORTH NAMING, since tonight has enough instances to be evidence rather than coincidence. Every PR I have held tonight was held for the same reason: something is silent that should speak. The phase override discarding a reality probe, the guard whose name promises more than it checks, the event field that cannot express "not measured", the cross-queue write with no line. None of them were wrong about what to do. All of them were wrong about saying so. That is worth carrying into the prompts — an instruction to state what a change does silently, and to justify each silence, would have caught all four before they reached me.
